question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x-b}, & x\le 1 \\ 4x-2, & x>1\end{aligned}
$$

is continuous at $x=1,$ find the value of the constant $b.$

$b=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
At $x=1,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}\sqrt{x-b} \\  & =\sqrt{1-b},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(4x-2) \\  & =4(1)-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) \\ \sqrt{1-b} & =2 \\ {(\sqrt{1-b})}^{2} & ={2}^{2} \\ 1-b & =4 \\ b & =1-4 \\ b & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
